messages:
Sam R.: hey team, heads-up — AcmeCorp is seeing a spike of 504s from hosted inference over the last ~25m. Customer reports streaming requests hang and then 504. They pasted a minimal repro and logs.

Sam R.: curl they ran:
```
curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```

Sam R.: response shows long time-to-first-byte then: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout

Sam R.: SDK version on their app is 1.3.2 (node). They said they refresh tokens on every user request (short-lived tokens from their auth) and use HTTP/2 multiplexing. Customer is on us-west1 region. Any quick mitigation to stop user-facing errors? :wave:

Jess (Support): thanks Sam. Can you paste the small repro and the raw SDK logs (with debug=network) next? Also what is the client concurrency (requests/sec) they saw?

Sam R.: concurrency ~10-20 RPS per process, multiple processes behind k8s HPA. Repro snippet from them (JS):
```
const token = await getShortLivedToken(); // they call per request
await client.generate({model:'gpt-xl',input:prompt,stream:true, auth: token});
```

Sam R.: SDK logs show repeated CONNECT/SETTINGS for the same upstream host and lots of connection creation around the 504 window.

Anya (Eng Runtime): interesting — sounds like connection reuse is failing and token refresh per request could be preventing persistent connections (auth header changes -> new connection per request + HTTP/2 stream window exhaustion). Can we check keepalive / conn pool metrics for that customer? Also does SDK 1.3.2 have a regression for HTTP/2 connection reuse? I think 1.4.0 had a fix.

Ingrid (Platform): confirmed increased connection churn in us-west1 between 17:30–17:55 UTC correlating with the 504 spike. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/usw1/edge-conns?from=17:20&to=18:00 (internal). CPU on edge proxies is fine, but active streams per connection jumped and we hit upstream windowed queueing.

Jess (Support): immediate customer-facing mitigations:
- ask Acme to cache tokens for a short TTL (e.g., 60s) instead of per-request refresh,
- or temporarily disable HTTP/2 multiplexing in SDK (fallback to HTTP/1.1) if they can,
- upgrade to SDK 1.4.0 (contains connection reuse and backoff fixes).

Sam R.: I've messaged customer with those three options and asked for logs. They asked if we can patch from our side.

Anya (Eng Runtime): on our side we can patch a short-term abort window increase for upstreams to avoid premature 504s, but that risks longer client hangs. Better to fix connection storm. I'll open an ops ticket to throttle new connection creation per tenant.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-904 for "us-west1 connection churn -> 504s (multi-tenant)". Priority: P2. Pager duty notified.

Ingrid (Platform): adding this tenant to a targeted rate-limit on new TLS sessions for the next 30m to dampen the fanout. I'll post a follow-up in 10m. :eyes:

Jess (Support): thanks — I'll keep Acme updated. Sam, paste the customer's debug logs when they arrive and mark the thread.

Sam R.: will do. Customer replied they can try the short token TTL cache as immediate test. I'll update when they confirm result. :thumbsup:
